comment: Foods USDA has no usable record for, estimated per 100 g and reviewed
before merge. Every row states the basis its numbers came from, because
the review is the only thing standing between an estimate and a calorie
count a cook believes. Add a row only with evidence of a real miss: an
ingredient the ops panel or a dry run recorded as skipped, and a probe
showing USDA genuinely has no record for it rather than one the matching
`id` is not a FoodData Central identifier. The 9000000 block is Ladle's
own; the evidence line names the source and the food, so these never

entries.name: garam masala
entries.basis: Unweighted mean of the six USDA SR Legacy spices a standard garam masala is built from: coriander seed (170922, 298 kcal), cumin seed (170923, 375), pepper black (170931, 251), cinnamon ground (171320, 247), cardamom (170919, 311), cloves ground (171321, 274). USDA has no garam masala record - its best answer is SMART SOUP, Indian Bean Masala (171181, 57 kcal). Proportions vary by house, so the mean is used rather than a weighted recipe; the six sit between 247 and 375 kcal, which bounds the error at well under a spoonful's worth.

entries.name: curry leaves
entries.basis: The published Indian food-composition figure for fresh Murraya koenigii leaves: 108 kcal, 6.1 g protein, 18.7 g carbohydrate, 1.0 g fat, 6.4 g fibre per 100 g. USDA has no record - it answers `curry leaves` with Drumstick leaves, raw (168416), a different plant, and `curry leaf` with beef curry. This is the least-backed row in the table: no laboratory record supports it and it is not a blend that can be averaged from one. Recipes use 1-15 g, so a 30% error here is a few kcal on a dish.

entries.name: ginger garlic paste
entries.basis: Equal parts of the two USDA SR Legacy records it is made from: Ginger root, raw (169231 - 80 kcal, 1.82 P, 17.8 C, 0.75 F, 2.0 fibre) and Garlic, raw (169230 - 149 kcal, 6.36 P, 33.1 C, 0.5 F, 2.1 fibre). USDA has no paste record; before the September 1 query fix it answered Almond paste, and after it answers Ginger root, raw alone, which silently drops the garlic. Jarred pastes are usually let down with water and oil and salted; this row is the plain 1:1 fresh blend, which is what a recipe means.

entries.name: tamarind paste
entries.basis: USDA Tamarinds, raw (167763 - 239 kcal, 2.8 P, 62.5 C, 0.6 F, 5.1 fibre) scaled by 0.8 for the water a commercial paste is let down with. The 0.8 is the one outright guess in this table: jars run from near-neat pulp to heavily diluted concentrate and their own labels land between roughly 150 and 240 kcal per 100 g. Deliberately not aliased to bare `tamarind` - USDA answers that correctly with Tamarind (2709269) and Tamarinds, raw (167763), and a curated row must not displace a real record.

entries.name: italian seasoning
entries.basis: Unweighted mean of the six USDA SR Legacy dried herbs the blend is made of: oregano (171328, 265 kcal), basil (171317, 233), thyme (170938, 276), rosemary (171333, 331), marjoram (170928, 271), sage ground (170935, 315). USDA has no record for the blend - it answers `italian seasoning` with Bread, Italian and Italian Ice. Two recipes in the September 2 dry run were skipped on it, at 1 g and 4 g.
